title: African leaders travel to Kyiv and St Petersburg on a peace mission
body:
In mid-June 2023, a delegation of African leaders carried out a self-declared peace mission, described as the first of its kind by African leaders, visiting Ukraine and then Russia. The group was led by South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and also included the presidents of Comoros, Senegal and Zambia, Egypt's prime minister, and top envoys from the Republic of Congo and Uganda. Other reports date the meetings in Kyiv and St Petersburg to 16 and 17 June 2023.

The delegation proposed de-escalation followed by peace negotiations. Ramaphosa said the war must be settled "through negotiations and through diplomatic means", and noted that it was hurting African economies because the continent relies on food and fertilizer from Russia and Ukraine.

In Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelensky asked the African leaders to press Russia to free political prisoners, including Crimeans held since 2014, and said talks were only possible if Russia withdrew from all Ukrainian territory. He noted Ukraine's ongoing counteroffensive. In St Petersburg, Putin said Russia was not giving up on negotiations with Ukraine, welcomed the leaders' "balanced stance" and said Russia responded positively to their proposal. African leaders were divided on whether to condemn Russia's invasion, and the United States had questioned South Africa's neutrality, alleging that it secretly supplied Russia with weapons in December 2022. Ramaphosa said he was investigating the allegations.
